a possible defect and a whole new feature 

please read, understand, and ONLY if appropriate fix all defects 
including any uncovered below 

**Verdict: confirmed.** I traced it through the slot machine's browser module by reading the code (I haven't run it in a browser).

## What happens

When you press the button and the server accepts it, the machine shows "Your press worked. This spin is yours." in the status line under the reels. That message is tied to one specific spin, but nothing ever ties it to that spin's lifetime.

When the reels stop, the message stays. When another visitor presses and a new spin starts, the message is still there, even though the new spin belongs to someone else. You end up watching a stranger's spin under a line claiming it's yours.

## Why it happens

The status line is only ever changed by your own actions:

- pressing the button (success, "someone else pressed first", "slow down", or "could not reach the server")
- switching auto spin on or off

Everything driven by the server, such as a new spin starting, reels stopping, or a result landing in the list, never touches it. The code does clear the big verdict banner ("Jackpot!", "Straight up", etc.) when any new spin begins, so the author clearly meant per-spin messages to reset. The status line was simply missed.

## What the user sees

- After your spin settles, "This spin is yours" lingers indefinitely.
- When someone else's spin starts and finishes, the message is now false. The result appears in the list without the "Your press" tag, which contradicts the status line.
- It stays until you press again, toggle auto spin, or leave the page.
- The same applies to the other status messages: "Slow down a little", "Could not reach the server", and the auto spin on/off notes also linger long after they're relevant.
- A screen reader user is affected too. The line is only announced when its text changes, and since a repeat success sets identical text, it isn't re-announced, which adds to the confusion.

## Why tests didn't catch it

The end-to-end test checks that the message appears after a press, and that the other browser sees the result without the "yours" tag. Nothing checks that the message goes away afterward.

## Suggested fix (in words)

Clear the status line whenever a new spin begins, the same way the verdict banner is already cleared. Optionally also clear it when your own spin finishes, or after a short timeout, since "This spin is yours" is most useful while the reels are turning. Transient errors like "Slow down" would ideally expire on a timer.

## A smaller sibling

The latency page has the same pattern: "Done. Your result is at the top of the list." stays after other people's tests arrive. It's less misleading there, but it's the same missing reset.

please read, understand, and ONLY if appropriate fix all defects

Shared files
I’ve confirmed the defect and fixed it, built the new Read page, and fixed the mobile nav. 40 files changed, so it’s a tar.gz above. It only has changed files, laid out from the repo root. Nothing needs deleting.

What I checked, and what I couldn’t run:

Checked: the app builds with warnings as errors, and all 177 JavaScript tests pass. I also ran the real app in a browser and repeated each new end-to-end check by hand: the slots and latency messages, the Read page, and no sideways scrolling at 320 and 390 px wide.
Not run: this sandbox can’t reach NuGet, so xunit, the integration tests and the Podman end-to-end tests haven’t run. The new parser and library tests did pass under a stand-in test runner. ReadPageTests.cs and the new end-to-end tests are only checked by reading them, not compiled. Please run scripts/run-all.sh first.
Browser script: the browser checks used the .NET 9 blazor.web.js, because the .NET 10 one wasn’t downloadable here.
The slots bug

The line under the machine now belongs to one spin. It clears when that spin stops or another spin starts.
If the server’s reply arrives after the spin has already started, the line still shows. If the spin has already landed, it doesn’t show at all.
Other notes (“Slow down”, “Could not reach the server”, auto spin on/off) clear after 6 seconds.
When the same message is shown twice in a row, it is cleared and written again, so screen readers announce it again.
Latency gets the same treatment: “Done” clears when someone else starts a test or their result lands.
One more I found: on the canvas, “It was just reset” or “The canvas is full” stayed after someone else reset. Any reset now clears it.
All of these have end-to-end tests that check the message goes away.
Mobile layout

Below 768 px, the nav moves to its own full-width row and wraps into even buttons. Desktop is unchanged.
No page scrolls sideways at 320 px, including a board post of 400 unbroken characters. An end-to-end test now checks every page at 320 and 390 px.
Long words anywhere on the site now wrap instead of overflowing.
Read page

/read redirects to a random article at /read/{id}. Each id comes from the article’s source URL, so links keep working if the file is reordered.
The server indexes nytimes.txt once (about 135 ms) and then reads only the one article a request needs. It re-indexes when the file changes.
528 articles in the file give 525 unique ones: 3 are exact copies filed under different names, and only the first is kept.
If the file is missing, too large or unreadable, the page says there’s nothing to read. An id that no longer exists says “Not available” with a link to a random article. Both show a normal page rather than an error, and I tested deleting and restoring the file while the app was running.
Layout: serif text at 17–19 px, a column about 38 characters of width wide, hyphenation, and bullet lists shown as real lists. It works in light and dark themes.
History: the browser keeps the last 1,000 articles opened (IndexedDB chaos-reading) and lists them at the bottom, newest first, with a read count and a “Reading now” marker. “Clear local history” on the About page clears it too.
Home, About, the README and the decision records are updated, including a new one, docs/adr/0024-reading.md.
Licensing: REUSE.toml marks every file in the repo as AGPL, which now includes the NYT text. You may want to look at that.

Shared files
I’ve confirmed the defect and fixed it, built the new Read page, and fixed the mobile nav. 40 files changed, so it’s a tar.gz above. It only has changed files, laid out from the repo root. Nothing needs deleting.

What I checked, and what I couldn’t run:

Checked: the app builds with warnings as errors, and all 177 JavaScript tests pass. I also ran the real app in a browser and repeated each new end-to-end check by hand: the slots and latency messages, the Read page, and no sideways scrolling at 320 and 390 px wide.
Not run: this sandbox can’t reach NuGet, so xunit, the integration tests and the Podman end-to-end tests haven’t run. The new parser and library tests did pass under a stand-in test runner. ReadPageTests.cs and the new end-to-end tests are only checked by reading them, not compiled. Please run scripts/run-all.sh first.
Browser script: the browser checks used the .NET 9 blazor.web.js, because the .NET 10 one wasn’t downloadable here.
The slots bug

The line under the machine now belongs to one spin. It clears when that spin stops or another spin starts.
If the server’s reply arrives after the spin has already started, the line still shows. If the spin has already landed, it doesn’t show at all.
Other notes (“Slow down”, “Could not reach the server”, auto spin on/off) clear after 6 seconds.
When the same message is shown twice in a row, it is cleared and written again, so screen readers announce it again.
Latency gets the same treatment: “Done” clears when someone else starts a test or their result lands.
One more I found: on the canvas, “It was just reset” or “The canvas is full” stayed after someone else reset. Any reset now clears it.
All of these have end-to-end tests that check the message goes away.
Mobile layout

Below 768 px, the nav moves to its own full-width row and wraps into even buttons. Desktop is unchanged.
No page scrolls sideways at 320 px, including a board post of 400 unbroken characters. An end-to-end test now checks every page at 320 and 390 px.
Long words anywhere on the site now wrap instead of overflowing.
Read page

/read redirects to a random article at /read/{id}. Each id comes from the article’s source URL, so links keep working if the file is reordered.
The server indexes nytimes.txt once (about 135 ms) and then reads only the one article a request needs. It re-indexes when the file changes.
528 articles in the file give 525 unique ones: 3 are exact copies filed under different names, and only the first is kept.
If the file is missing, too large or unreadable, the page says there’s nothing to read. An id that no longer exists says “Not available” with a link to a random article. Both show a normal page rather than an error, and I tested deleting and restoring the file while the app was running.
Layout: serif text at 17–19 px, a column about 38 characters of width wide, hyphenation, and bullet lists shown as real lists. It works in light and dark themes.
History: the browser keeps the last 1,000 articles opened (IndexedDB chaos-reading) and lists them at the bottom, newest first, with a read count and a “Reading now” marker. “Clear local history” on the About page clears it too.
Home, About, the README and the decision records are updated, including a new one, docs/adr/0024-reading.md.
Licensing: REUSE.toml marks every file in the repo as AGPL, which now includes the NYT text. You may want to look at that.

Ran 6 commands
The fault was in the test I added, not in the app. Both test pages run from the same network address, and the test config lets each network start one test per second. With every outside request blocked, the first test finishes in a few milliseconds. So the second page clicked “Run test” less than a second after the first test started, and the server refused it with “A test ran from your network recently”. That message cleared itself after 6 seconds, which is why the failure snapshot shows an empty status and an enabled button.

I reproduced it against the app here. Clicking straight away gave that refusal and no second test; waiting 1.5 seconds first made the second test run and land. The fix is that 1.5-second wait before the second page clicks, the same wait the new canvas test uses. Only this file changes; I haven’t re-run the full end-to-end suite.

tests/Chaos.E2E/LatencyTests.cs

csharp
using Microsoft.Playwright;
using static Microsoft.Playwright.Assertions;

namespace Chaos.E2E;

public sealed class LatencyTests(BrowserFixture browser) : IClassFixture<BrowserFixture>
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task ATestReachesEveryoneAndUnlocksAutoRun()
    {
        await using var firstContext = await OfflineContextAsync();
        await using var secondContext = await OfflineContextAsync();
        var tester = await firstContext.NewPageAsync();
        await tester.GotoAsync("/about");
        await tester.EvaluateAsync("() => localStorage.setItem('chaos-latency-runs', '9')");
        await OpenAsync(tester);
        var watcher = await secondContext.NewPageAsync();
        await OpenAsync(watcher);

        var auto = tester.GetByRole(AriaRole.Button, new() { Name = "Auto run" });
        await Expect(auto).ToBeHiddenAsync();
        await tester.GetByRole(AriaRole.Button, new() { Name = "Run test" }).ClickAsync();

        var mine = tester.Locator("#latency-feed .msg.mine").First;
        await Expect(mine).ToBeVisibleAsync(new() { Timeout = 30_000 });
        await Expect(auto).ToBeVisibleAsync();
        await Expect(tester.Locator(".probe .status")).ToHaveTextAsync("Done. Your result is at the top of the list.");
        await Expect(tester.Locator(".probe tr[data-key='chaos'] .browser")).ToHaveTextAsync(new System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex("^\\d+ ms$"));

        var id = await mine.GetAttributeAsync("data-id") ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("The result has no id.");
        var seen = watcher.Locator($"#latency-feed .msg[data-id='{id}']");
        await Expect(seen).ToBeVisibleAsync();
        await Expect(seen.Locator(".yours")).ToHaveCountAsync(0);
        await seen.Locator("summary").ClickAsync();
        await Expect(seen.Locator("tbody tr")).ToHaveCountAsync(await tester.Locator(".probe tbody tr").CountAsync());
        await Expect(watcher.Locator("#latency-browser-fastest-empty")).ToBeVisibleAsync();
        await Expect(watcher.Locator("#latency-jackpot-winners-empty")).ToBeVisibleAsync();

        await watcher.WaitForTimeoutAsync(1500);
        var run = watcher.GetByRole(AriaRole.Button, new() { Name = "Run test" });
        await Expect(run).ToBeEnabledAsync(new() { Timeout = 10_000 });
        await run.ClickAsync();
        await Expect(watcher.Locator("#latency-feed .msg.mine").First).ToBeVisibleAsync(new() { Timeout = 30_000 });
        await Expect(watcher.Locator(".probe .status")).ToHaveTextAsync("Done. Your result is at the top of the list.");
        await Expect(tester.Locator(".probe .status")).ToBeEmptyAsync();
    }

    private async Task<IBrowserContext> OfflineContextAsync()
    {
        var context = await browser.NewContextAsync();
        await context.RouteAsync(url => !url.StartsWith(BrowserFixture.BaseUrl, StringComparison.Ordinal), route => route.AbortAsync());
        return context;
    }

    private static async Task OpenAsync(IPage page)
    {
        await page.GotoAsync("/latency");
        await Expect(page.Locator(".probe[data-ready]")).ToBeVisibleAsync();
    }
}

GET /read/e0220c87e871 undefined
Host: chaos-eu.velixir.run
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:159.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/159.0
Accept: text/html; blazor-enhanced-nav=on
Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd

Read memory, ran a command, used a tool
The HAR confirms it. /read only breaks when you reach it by clicking a link inside the app.

What the HAR shows

If you type or reload chaos.velixir.run/read, the browser does a normal page load. It follows the 302 to chaos-eu.velixir.run/read/…, gets a 200, and the page works.
If you click into /read from another page, Blazor’s enhanced navigation fetches it in the background instead (the request has Accept: text/html; blazor-enhanced-nav=on). That fetch also gets the 302 to the other host, chaos-eu, and comes back with status 0. That’s the NS_ERROR_DOM_BAD_URI you’re seeing.
Why the fetch fails

A background fetch can’t follow a redirect to another site here, for two reasons:

Your CSP has connect-src 'self', and chaos-eu.velixir.run isn’t on the list, so Firefox blocks the redirected request.
Even if the CSP allowed it, the request would also need CORS on chaos-eu. Blazor would then try to swap a page from another site into the current one, which isn’t what you want.
The 302 comes from your edge proxy (x-served-by: velixir-edge), not from Blazor. Blazor never gets the chance to handle the redirect itself.

Fixes, any one will do:

Turn off enhanced navigation for links to /read:
razor
   <NavLink href="read" data-enhance-nav="false">Read</NavLink>
The browser then does a normal page load, which follows the redirect fine.

Make the edge redirect in a way Blazor understands. When the request’s Accept contains blazor-enhanced-nav=on, return a 200 with the header blazor-enhanced-nav-redirect-location: https://chaos-eu.velixir.run/read/<id> instead of a 302. Blazor’s script should then do a full page load to that URL. I’m going from memory on that header, so check it against the Blazor source for your version before relying on it. Keep the 302 for every other request.
Do the redirect inside the app. Drop it at the edge and call NavigationManager.NavigateTo(url, forceLoad: true) in the /read page. Blazor then handles the redirect itself during enhanced navigation.
Option 1 is the quickest. Option 2 keeps enhanced navigation and fixes it for every page the edge redirects to another host. Don’t add chaos-eu to connect-src: that only gets you past the first block and leaves the CORS problem.


Automatically approve is on. Claude runs on its own and pauses if anything looks unsafe. This includes using your connectors and Claude in Chrome, unless you turn them off. Learn more
